raft_ocean.story.log.0:
RADIO TOWER — Ivo, first watch

The stairs rang under my boots long after I stopped climbing. Below us, the sea covered the road we had followed yesterday. Mara tied three strips of canvas to the railing so another boat would know someone had reached the tower. Sela counted our tins twice, then divided the water into equal cups. Nobody asked how long that would last.

The receiver woke when I cleaned the salt from its contacts. Most channels held only rain. One carried three knocks, a pause, then three more. Mara answered with the tower lamp. The distant light answered back. We copied its bearing onto the back of a supply list: Glasswatch.

I left the original list beneath this journal. It has six names, although only three of us climbed these stairs. We cannot reach every missing person at once. Tonight we can keep one light on. If you find this after we leave, take the spare wire and keep listening.

NEXT: Find Glasswatch and Mara's lookout journal. Its lamp is above the coastal landing.
raft_ocean.story.log.1:
GLASSWATCH — Mara, lookout keeper

For nine nights I counted a light beyond the rain. On the tenth it answered our tower signal: three flashes, a pause, three more. At Glasswatch we found a cold kettle, a folded blanket and a watch chart with the last shift left blank. Whoever maintained that light had left before us. I filled the empty square with our arrival time.

We spread Ivo's charts across the lookout table and marked every reply. Sela pressed a leaf between two pages so the ink would not stick. By morning the table held bearings, water rings and the outline of a coast none of us remembered. Ivo insisted the northern channel was still safe. I wanted to believe him.

Then our fresh water ran low. Sela asked for two days at Garden Relay; her seedlings had roots now. I stayed beside the ladder until dawn, listening to an empty channel. The watch chart remains on the desk. A blank shift is not proof that nobody is coming.

NEXT: Find Garden Relay and Sela's journal. Take seeds if its glasshouse survives, but leave something for another boat.
raft_ocean.story.log.2:
GARDEN RELAY — Sela, seed keeper

The first green shoot grew in a cracked cup. Mara carried it here like a rescued passenger. We planted rows under glass and caught rain in the old cauldron. Ivo repaired the roof while arguing that we should leave. Each evening he checked the seedlings before returning to the receiver. I pretended not to notice.

A supply boat called from the northern channel. I packed a tin of seeds for its crew and gave Ivo our newest route sketch. The storm arrived before the boat did. It took the relay mast; the garden survived. We listened for their engine until the rain stopped.

Before leaving, I moved our charts into Echo Vault. The relay key stays here for anyone returning hungry. Its switches remember our night watch: Mara awake, the empty middle bunk, Ivo awake. Facing the seal: LEFT ON, MIDDLE OFF, RIGHT ON. Use the key afterward.

The tin by the planting bench is empty because we sent its seeds away, not because we gave up. If the boat reached shelter, perhaps those seeds are already growing.

NEXT: Find Echo Vault. Ivo left the supply boat's last bearing with the corrected charts.
raft_ocean.story.log.3:
ECHO VAULT — Ivo, chart maker

I built this room to keep our maps dry. Then I caught myself locking it as though ink belonged to me. Mara asked what a safe route was worth if nobody could read it. We filled the shelves with copies. Sela numbered them on scraps of seed packets because we had run out of labels.

The northern passage was my mistake. I trusted a shoreline the storm had changed. The supply crew followed the line I drew; their last call mentioned shallow water and a broken rudder. After that, silence. I crossed out the route so heavily that the paper tore. Mara kept the final bearing: Ember Beacon.

On the next chart I wrote what I had measured and what I had merely guessed. They are different things. The ledger records water, repairs and names of crews who passed through. One page is missing from its binding. I assumed the supply crew took it for a receipt. Now I am less certain.

NEXT: Sail to Ember Beacon and climb to the lantern room. Its keeper may have recorded where the missing boat landed.

raft_ocean.story.log.4:
EMBER BEACON — Mara, last lighthouse watch

The supply boat arrived with its sail wrapped around the mast. Two passengers, an empty tank and Sela's seed tin lashed beneath a bench. Their rudder had split in the channel. They followed our flashes with a paddle until the beacon keeper pulled them into the cove. We gave them the cottage and heated water before asking for their names.

One passenger handed Ivo a page from his ledger, folded around a dry match. The margins held repair counts in a different hand. Below them someone had written: KEEP A COPY ASHORE. Neither passenger knew who added it. They had found the page tucked beneath their water tank.

Ivo wanted to shut down the light and save its copper for our engine. That evening he climbed the ladder carrying a new coil. He never apologized in words. The lantern burned until sunrise.

We stocked the cottage for another arrival and took the rescued crew to Tideworks Haven. I copied the strange handwriting before we left. A useful warning can still have an unknown author.

NEXT: Follow the signal to Tideworks Haven. Sela kept our departure notes beside the repaired tanks.
raft_ocean.story.log.5:
TIDEWORKS HAVEN — Sela, departure morning

The pier was too narrow for everyone, so Ivo extended it. The workshop smelled of wet timber and hot iron. Mara hung lamps along the posts while our passengers patched the tank seams. At supper we used the cracked cup to measure flour. It finally held something that did not leak.

We compared the loose ledger page with our own records. Its repair counts matched work we had done here, including a tank fixed that morning. The page had reached Ember Beacon before those repairs happened. Ivo checked the dates twice. Mara asked us to keep the original dry.

We stored a copy with the corrected charts at Starfall Archive. The harbor key opens its seal. Facing it: LEFT ON, MIDDLE OFF, RIGHT ON. Use the key afterward. The receiver's new bearing should lead you to the archive and its observatory.

We are leaving together. The seed tins and spare tools remain for a late crew. I have written everyone's name in the ledger, leaving space beneath them. We do not yet know whether that space is an invitation or a warning.

NEXT: Visit Starfall Archive. Our latest copied entry records the signal we heard from its observatory.
raft_ocean.story.log.6:
STARFALL ARCHIVE — An unfinished transmission

MARA: From the observatory we saw the coastal lights form a chain. Beyond its final light the receiver caught a different rhythm. A voice said 'bring the ledger' before the storm swallowed the rest. It answered again after we switched our beacon off. This was not our own signal returning.

IVO: I compared the voice with the tower notes. The pauses match, but the bearing drifts east whenever the clouds close in. The loose page describes repairs made after it was found. A wrong date might explain one entry, not every mark. I have filed the page between our measured charts and left the guessed route blank. Nobody should sail into danger because I wanted an answer.

SELA: The cracked cup is aboard. The seeds are dry. We left this copy so the next crew can compare what they hear with what we heard. Mara keeps watch; Ivo listens. We are sailing east, but we do not know who is calling, why they know our repairs, or which ledger they expect us to bring.

The last line of the transmission may have been 'leave one light'. It may have been a name. Until another message reaches us, the channel remains open.

raft_ocean.exploration.log.0: Survey 18: The observatory soil is rich in clay, but the green current carries our markers away. The Broken Keel holds spare iron. Follow the coral shelf to the Grotto, or take the smoke-bearing to Basalt Refuge. Three routes, no agreed destination. We left the receiver tuned for whoever comes next.
raft_ocean.exploration.log.1: Refuge ledger: Iron veins kept our tools alive; they did not bring the fleet home. Orchard Cove traded food for our ore. The Drowned Court guards old metal, while Chart Vault stores fragments of a route beyond this sea. No fragment proves the crossing safe. Keep a copy and choose your own course.
raft_ocean.exploration.log.2: Orchard letter: Take ripe carrots and leave a row for the next crew. We sent a survey east and a supply boat toward the Broken Keel. Neither returned, but last night the receiver answered with an unfamiliar voice. Our map ends at Chart Vault. The ocean does not.
